#Alpha Diversity Analysis#
```{r}
#--------------------------------------------------
# SUBSETTING TO ONLY THE SAMPLES WE WANT TO ANALYSE
#--------------------------------------------------
bac.no.norm <- BSpermosphere_RDS_NoNorm %>%
  subset_samples(Trt != "Soybean Epiphytes") %>%
  phyloseq::filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, TRUE) 

bac.rare <- BSpermosphere_RDS_Rareified %>%
  subset_samples(Trt != "Soybean Epiphytes") %>%
  phyloseq::filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, TRUE) 

bac.CSS.norm <- BSpermosphere_RDS_CSS %>%
  subset_samples(Trt != "Soybean Epiphytes") %>%
  phyloseq::filter_taxa(function(x) sum(x) > 0, TRUE) 

#--------------------------------------------------
# FACTORS
#--------------------------------------------------

sample_data(bac.no.norm)$Time <- factor(
  sample_data(bac.no.norm)$Time,
  levels = c("Planting","17hrs","V2")
)

sample_data(bac.rare)$Time <- factor(
  sample_data(bac.rare)$Time,
  levels = c("Planting","17hrs","V2")
)

#--------------------------------------------------
# ALPHA DIVERSITY FUNCTION
#--------------------------------------------------

get_alpha <- function(ps){

  # ---------------------------
  # Standard alpha diversity
  # ---------------------------

  alpha <- estimate_richness(
    ps,
    measures = c(
      "Observed",
      "Shannon",
      "Simpson",
      "InvSimpson"
    )
  )

  # ---------------------------
  # Pielou's evenness
  # ---------------------------

  alpha$even <- alpha$Shannon /
    log(alpha$Observed)

  # ---------------------------
  # OTU table
  # ---------------------------

  otu <- t(as(otu_table(ps), "matrix"))

  # Relative abundances
  relabund <- sweep(
    otu,
    1,
    rowSums(otu),
    "/"
  )

  # ---------------------------
  # Hill numbers
  # ---------------------------

  alpha$Hill0 <- hillR::hill_taxa(
    otu,
    q = 0
  )

  alpha$Hill1 <- hillR::hill_taxa(
    otu,
    q = 1
  )

  alpha$Hill2 <- hillR::hill_taxa(
    otu,
    q = 2
  )

  alpha$Hill3 <- hillR::hill_taxa(
    otu,
    q = 3
  )

  # ---------------------------
  # Dominance metrics
  # ---------------------------

  # Berger-Parker dominance
  # = relative abundance of most dominant taxon

  alpha$BergerParker <- apply(
    relabund,
    1,
    max
  )

  # Effective Berger-Parker
  # Interpretable as the number of equally
  # abundant taxa represented by the dominant taxon

  alpha$InvBergerParker <-
    1 / alpha$BergerParker

  # ---------------------------
  # Top-N abundance
  # ---------------------------

  alpha$Top5 <- apply(
    relabund,
    1,
    function(x){

      x <- sort(
        x,
        decreasing = TRUE
      )

      sum(head(x, 5))

    }
  )

  alpha$Top10 <- apply(
    relabund,
    1,
    function(x){

      x <- sort(
        x,
        decreasing = TRUE
      )

      sum(head(x, 10))

    }
  )

  # ---------------------------
  # Gini coefficient
  # ---------------------------

  alpha$Gini <- apply(
    relabund,
    1,
    function(x){

      ineq::Gini(x)

    }
  )

  # ---------------------------
  # Faith's PD
  # ---------------------------

  pd_out <- picante::pd(
    otu,
    phy_tree(ps),
    include.root = FALSE
  )

  alpha$PD <- pd_out$PD

  # ---------------------------
  # Metadata
  # ---------------------------

  alpha$Tube <- rownames(alpha)

  alpha <- left_join(
    alpha,
    data.frame(sample_data(ps)),
    by = "Tube"
  )

  return(alpha)

}

#==================================================
# CALCULATE ALPHA DIVERSITY METRICS
#==================================================

# Alpha diversity metrics calculated from:
#  - Non-normalized counts 
#  - Rarefied counts (available if richness analyses based on
#    rarefaction are desired)
alpha_dat_nonorm <- get_alpha(bac.no.norm)
alpha_dat_rare   <- get_alpha(bac.rare)

# Before doing any analysis, does sequencing depth matter?
ggplot(
  alpha_dat_nonorm,
  aes(
    x = sample_sums(bac.no.norm),
    y = Hill1
  )
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

# Sequencing depth clearly has a large effect on all alpha diversity metrics. 
cor.test(
  log(sample_sums(bac.no.norm)),
  alpha_dat_nonorm$Hill1
)
```

To evaluate the effects of soil steaming, plant association, and developmental stage on alpha diversity, habitats were grouped into either bulk soil or plant-associated categories. Richness, Pielou's evenness, and Faith's phylogenetic diversity were modeled as functions of treatment (steamed vs. non-steamed), habitat, developmental stage, and all interaction terms. Richness was analyzed using a Gaussian model of log-transformed observed richness, Pielou's evenness was analyzed using beta regression, and Faith's phylogenetic diversity was analyzed using a Gaussian linear model. Model assumptions were evaluated using simulated DHARMa residuals. Type III ANOVA was used to assess the significance of main effects and interactions.

```{r}
#==================================================
# ALPHA DIVERSITY ANALYSIS
# Purpose:
#   1. Collapse habitats into Bulk Soil vs Plant-associated
#   2. Test effects of steaming treatment (Trt),
#      habitat type (Habitat), and developmental stage (Time)
#   3. Fit separate models for Richness, Evenness, and Faith's PD
#   4. Evaluate model diagnostics using DHARMa
#   5. Extract ANOVA tables for each metric
#   6. Combine results into a single supplemental table
#==================================================

#==================================================
# CREATE HABITAT VARIABLE
#==================================================
# Collapse Spermosphere and Rhizosphere into a single
# "Plant-associated" category for testing overall plant effects.

alpha_dat_rare <- alpha_dat_rare %>%
  mutate(
    Habitat = ifelse(
      Type == "Bulk.Soil",
      "Bulk Soil",
      "Plant-associated"
    ),
    Habitat = factor(
      Habitat,
      levels = c("Bulk Soil", "Plant-associated")
    )
  )

alpha_dat_nonorm <- alpha_dat_nonorm %>%
  mutate(
    Habitat = ifelse(
      Type == "Bulk.Soil",
      "Bulk Soil",
      "Plant-associated"
    ),
    Habitat = factor(
      Habitat,
      levels = c("Bulk Soil", "Plant-associated")
    )
  )

#==================================================
# RICHNESS MODEL
#==================================================
# Compare Gaussian models fit to raw and log-transformed richness.
# The log-transformed model was retained based on substantially
# improved AIC and acceptable diagnostic performance.

rich.mod.log <- glmmTMB(
  log(Observed) ~ Trt * Habitat * Time,
  family = gaussian(),
  data = alpha_dat_rare
)

rich.mod.raw <- glmmTMB(
  Observed ~ Trt * Habitat * Time,
  family = gaussian(),
  data = alpha_dat_rare
)

# Compare model fit
AIC(rich.mod.log, rich.mod.raw)

# DHARMa residual diagnostics
sim_rich <- simulateResiduals(
  fittedModel = rich.mod.log,
  n = 1000
)

plot(sim_rich)

testResiduals(sim_rich)
testUniformity(sim_rich)
testDispersion(sim_rich)
testOutliers(sim_rich)

# Type III ANOVA
rich_anova <- car::Anova(
  rich.mod.log,
  type = 3
)

rich_anova

# Convert ANOVA table to data frame
anova_df_rich <- as.data.frame(rich_anova)

anova_df_rich$Term <- rownames(anova_df_rich)

anova_df_rich <- anova_df_rich %>%
  relocate(Term) %>%
  mutate(Metric = "Richness")

#==================================================
# EVENNESS MODEL
#==================================================
# Evenness is bounded between 0 and 1, so beta regression
# is used. The dispersion (phi) parameter is modeled as a
# function of treatment, habitat, and time.

even.mod <- glmmTMB(
  even ~ Trt * Habitat * Time,
  dispformula = ~ Trt * Habitat * Time,
  family = beta_family(),
  data = alpha_dat_nonorm
)

# DHARMa diagnostics
sim_even <- simulateResiduals(
  fittedModel = even.mod,
  n = 1000
)

plot(sim_even)

testResiduals(sim_even)
testUniformity(sim_even)
testDispersion(sim_even)
testOutliers(sim_even)

# Type III ANOVA
even_anova <- car::Anova(
  even.mod,
  type = 3
)

even_anova

# Convert ANOVA table to data frame
anova_df_even <- as.data.frame(even_anova)

anova_df_even$Term <- rownames(anova_df_even)

anova_df_even <- anova_df_even %>%
  relocate(Term) %>%
  mutate(Metric = "Evenness")

#==================================================
# FOLLOW-UP CONTRASTS FOR SIGNIFICANT INTERACTION
#==================================================
# Evaluate treatment effects within each habitat and
# developmental stage combination.

even.emm <- emmeans(
  even.mod,
  pairwise ~ Trt | Habitat | Time,
  adjust = "BH"
)

even.emm

#==================================================
# FAITH'S PHYLOGENETIC DIVERSITY
#==================================================
# Faith's PD was modeled using a standard Gaussian linear model.

pd.mod <- lm(
  PD ~ Trt * Habitat * Time,
  data = alpha_dat_nonorm
)

# DHARMa diagnostics
sim_pd <- simulateResiduals(
  fittedModel = pd.mod,
  n = 1000
)

plot(sim_pd)

testResiduals(sim_pd)
testUniformity(sim_pd)
testDispersion(sim_pd)
testOutliers(sim_pd)

# Type III ANOVA
pd_anova <- car::Anova(
  pd.mod,
  type = 3
)

pd_anova

# Convert ANOVA table to data frame
anova_df_pd <- as.data.frame(pd_anova)

anova_df_pd$Term <- rownames(anova_df_pd)

anova_df_pd <- anova_df_pd %>%
  relocate(Term) %>%
  mutate(Metric = "Faith's PD")

#==================================================
# COMBINE ALL ANOVA TABLES
#==================================================
# Standardize Richness, Evenness, and Faith's PD results
# into a single supplemental table.

rich_tbl <- anova_df_rich %>%
  transmute(
    Metric = "Richness",
    Term,
    Df,
    Test = "Chi-square",
    Statistic = Chisq,
    Pvalue = `Pr(>Chisq)`
  )

even_tbl <- anova_df_even %>%
  transmute(
    Metric = "Evenness",
    Term,
    Df,
    Test = "Chi-square",
    Statistic = Chisq,
    Pvalue = `Pr(>Chisq)`
  )

pd_tbl <- anova_df_pd %>%
  transmute(
    Metric = "Faith's PD",
    Term,
    Df,
    Test = "F",
    Statistic = `F value`,
    Pvalue = `Pr(>F)`
  )

alpha_anova <- bind_rows(
  rich_tbl,
  even_tbl,
  pd_tbl
) %>%
  filter(
    !Term %in% c("(Intercept)", "Residuals")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Statistic = round(Statistic, 3),
    Pvalue = round(Pvalue, 3)
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

rownames(alpha_anova) <- NULL

# Final supplemental table
alpha_anova

# Optional export
# write.csv(alpha_anova,
#           "AlphaDiversity_ANOVA.csv",
#           row.names = FALSE)
```

To directly quantify plant effects relative to the surrounding soil community, alpha-diversity metrics were converted to delta values, calculated as the difference between plant-associated and bulk-soil communities (Plant-associated − Bulk soil) within each treatment, developmental stage, and replicate. Positive values indicate higher diversity or dominance within plant-associated habitats relative to bulk soil, whereas negative values indicate lower values in plant-associated habitats. Delta metrics were subsequently analyzed as a function of steaming treatment, developmental stage, and their interaction.

```{r}
#==================================================
# DELTA ALPHA-DIVERSITY METRICS
#==================================================
# Purpose:
# Calculate the difference between plant-associated and
# bulk-soil communities within each treatment, time point,
# and replicate. Delta values are defined as:
#
# Delta = Plant-associated - Bulk Soil
#
# Positive delta values indicate enrichment within plant-
# associated habitats, whereas negative values indicate
# reduced diversity or increased dominance relative to
# the corresponding bulk-soil community.

delta_alpha <- alpha_dat_rare %>%

  # Classify samples as bulk soil or plant-associated
  mutate(
    HabitatClass = ifelse(
      Type == "Bulk.Soil",
      "Bulk",
      "Plant"
    )
  ) %>%

  # Calculate mean alpha-diversity metrics within each
  # treatment × time × habitat × replicate grouping
  group_by(
    Trt,
    Time,
    HabitatClass,
    Rep
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    # Traditional alpha-diversity metrics
    Richness = mean(Observed),
    Evenness = mean(even),
    PD = mean(PD),

    # Hill numbers
    Hill1 = mean(Hill1),
    Hill2 = mean(Hill2),
    Hill3 = mean(Hill3),

    # Simpson-based diversity metrics
    Simpson = mean(Simpson),
    InvSimpson = mean(InvSimpson),
    SimpsonConcentration = mean(1 - Simpson),

    # Dominance metrics
    BergerParker = mean(BergerParker),
    InvBergerParker = mean(InvBergerParker),

    # Relative abundance of dominant taxa
    Top5 = mean(Top5),
    Top10 = mean(Top10),

    # Community inequality
    Gini = mean(Gini),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  # Create separate Bulk and Plant columns for each metric
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = HabitatClass,
    values_from = c(
      Richness,
      Evenness,
      PD,
      Hill1,
      Hill2,
      Hill3,
      Simpson,
      InvSimpson,
      SimpsonConcentration,
      BergerParker,
      InvBergerParker,
      Top5,
      Top10,
      Gini
    )
  ) %>%

  # Calculate plant-associated minus bulk-soil differences
  mutate(

    # Diversity metrics
    DeltaRichness = Richness_Plant - Richness_Bulk,
    DeltaEvenness = Evenness_Plant - Evenness_Bulk,
    DeltaPD = PD_Plant - PD_Bulk,

    # Hill numbers
    DeltaHill1 = Hill1_Plant - Hill1_Bulk,
    DeltaHill2 = Hill2_Plant - Hill2_Bulk,
    DeltaHill3 = Hill3_Plant - Hill3_Bulk,

    # Simpson metrics
    DeltaSimpson =
      Simpson_Plant - Simpson_Bulk,

    DeltaInvSimpson =
      InvSimpson_Plant - InvSimpson_Bulk,

    DeltaSimpsonConcentration =
      SimpsonConcentration_Plant -
      SimpsonConcentration_Bulk,

    # Dominance metrics
    DeltaBergerParker =
      BergerParker_Plant -
      BergerParker_Bulk,

    DeltaInvBergerParker =
      InvBergerParker_Plant -
      InvBergerParker_Bulk,

    # Dominance of abundant taxa
    DeltaTop5 =
      Top5_Plant - Top5_Bulk,

    DeltaTop10 =
      Top10_Plant - Top10_Bulk,

    # Community inequality
    DeltaGini =
      Gini_Plant - Gini_Bulk
  )

#==================================================
# DELTA RICHNESS
#==================================================
# Test whether steaming alters the magnitude of plant
# effects on richness across developmental stages.

rich.lm <- lm(
  DeltaRichness ~ Trt * Time,
  data = delta_alpha
)

# Evaluate model assumptions
sim.rich <- simulateResiduals(rich.lm)

plot(sim.rich)

# Type I ANOVA
anova(rich.lm)

# Pairwise comparisons among time points
rich.emm <- emmeans(
  rich.lm,
  pairwise ~ Time,
  adjust = "BH"
)

rich.emm

#==================================================
# DELTA EVENNESS
#==================================================
# Test whether steaming alters plant effects on
# community evenness throughout plant development.

even.lm <- lm(
  DeltaEvenness ~ Trt * Time,
  data = delta_alpha
)

# Residual diagnostics
sim.even <- simulateResiduals(even.lm)

plot(sim.even)

# Overall ANOVA
anova(even.lm)

# Treatment comparisons within each developmental stage
even.emm <- emmeans(
  even.lm,
  pairwise ~ Trt | Time,
  adjust = "BH"
)

even.emm

#==================================================
# DELTA FAITH'S PHYLOGENETIC DIVERSITY
#==================================================
# Test whether steaming alters plant-driven changes
# in phylogenetic diversity through time.

pd.mod <- lm(
  DeltaPD ~ Trt * Time,
  data = delta_alpha
)

# Diagnostic plots
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(pd.mod)
dev.off()

# Overall ANOVA
anova(pd.mod)
```


```{r}

# Most dominant taxon in each sample
dom_taxa <- microbiome::dominant(
  bac.rare
)

#==================================================
# IDENTIFY OTUs THAT ARE DOMINANT IN ≥1 SAMPLE
#==================================================

# Relative abundance phyloseq object
ps.rel <- transform_sample_counts(
  bac.rare,
  function(x) x / sum(x)
)

# Dominant OTU in each sample
dom_taxa <- dominant(
  ps.rel,
  level = "OTU"
)

# Unique set of dominant OTUs
otu.keep <- unique(dom_taxa)

# Alternatively, only keep OTUs dominant in >= 3 samples
# freq <- table(dom_taxa)
# otu.keep <- names(freq[freq >= 3])

#==================================================
# SUBSET TO DOMINANT OTUS
#==================================================

ps.dom <- prune_taxa(
  otu.keep,
  ps.rel
)

# Melt to dataframe
plot.df <- psmelt(ps.dom)

#==================================================
# CREATE INFORMATIVE TAXON LABELS
#==================================================

plot.df$Taxon <- ifelse(
  is.na(plot.df$Genus) | plot.df$Genus == "",
  plot.df$OTU,
  paste0(plot.df$Genus, " (", plot.df$OTU, ")")
)

#==================================================
# SUMMARIZE MEAN RELATIVE ABUNDANCE
#==================================================

plot.sum <- plot.df %>%
  mutate(
    HabitatClass = ifelse(
      Type == "Bulk.Soil",
      "Bulk Soil",
      "Plant-Associated"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    Trt,
    Time,
    HabitatClass,
    Taxon
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Abundance = mean(Abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Order timepoints
plot.sum$Time <- factor(
  plot.sum$Time,
  levels = c(
    "Planting",
    "17hrs",
    "V2"
  )
)

# Order taxa by overall abundance
tax.order <- plot.sum %>%
  group_by(Taxon) %>%
  summarise(
    TotalAbundance = sum(Abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(TotalAbundance)) %>%
  pull(Taxon)

plot.sum$Taxon <- factor(
  plot.sum$Taxon,
  levels = tax.order
)

#==================================================
# STACKED BAR CHART
#==================================================

p_dom <- ggplot(
  plot.sum,
  aes(
    x = Time,
    y = Abundance,
    fill = Taxon
  )
) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_grid(
    HabitatClass ~ Trt
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent_format()
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean Relative Abundance",
    fill = "Dominant OTUs"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tol20) +
  guides(
  fill = guide_legend(
    ncol = 2,
    byrow = TRUE
  )
) +
  theme(
  axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 45,
    hjust = 1,
    vjust = 1
  ),
  legend.position = "bottom"
)
p_dom

plot_delta <- function(dat, metric, ylab){

  ggplot(
    dat,
    aes(
      x = Time,
      y = .data[[metric]],
      color = Trt,
      group = Trt
    )
  ) +

    geom_hline(
      yintercept = 0,
      linetype = 2,
      color = "grey50"
    ) +

    geom_jitter(
      width = 0.08,
      alpha = 0.5,
      size = 1.5
    ) +

    stat_summary(
      fun = mean,
      geom = "line",
      linewidth = 1
    ) +

    stat_summary(
      fun = mean,
      geom = "point",
      size = 3
    ) +

    stat_summary(
      fun.data = mean_cl_normal,
      geom = "errorbar",
      width = 0.1
    ) +

    scale_color_manual(values = cbbPalette) +

    theme_classic() +

    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = ylab,
      color = "Treatment"
    )
}

even.plot <- plot_delta(
  delta_alpha,
  "DeltaEvenness",
  "Δ Pielou's Evenness\n(Plant-associated - Bulk Soil)"
)

(even.plot | p_dom)
```

## Bacterial Beta-diversity
### Global analysis 
```{r}
# Create Bray distance matrix
bac.bray <- phyloseq::distance(bac.CSS.norm, method = "bray")

# Create Weighted UniFrac distance matrix
bac.wunifrac <- phyloseq::distance(
  bac.CSS.norm,
  method = "wunifrac"
)

# Metadata
cssbac.meta.data <- data.frame(sample_data(bac.CSS.norm))

# Create habitat variable
cssbac.meta.data$Habitat_Stage <- with(
  cssbac.meta.data,
  paste(Time, Type, sep = "_")
)

# Optional nicer labels
cssbac.meta.data$Habitat_Stage <- recode(
  cssbac.meta.data$Habitat_Stage,
  "Planting_Bulk.Soil"    = "Planting_Bulk",
  "Planting_Spermosphere" = "Planting_Spermosphere",
  "17hrs_Bulk.Soil"       = "17hr_Bulk",
  "17hrs_Spermosphere"    = "17hr_Spermosphere",
  "V2_Bulk.Soil"          = "V2_Bulk",
  "V2_Rhizosphere"        = "V2_Rhizosphere"
)

# PERMANOVA
set.seed(12345)

brayperm <- adonis2(
  bac.bray ~ Trt * Habitat_Stage,
  data = cssbac.meta.data,
  by = "term"
)

wuniperm <- adonis2(
  bac.wunifrac ~ Trt * Habitat_Stage,
  data = cssbac.meta.data,
  by = "term"
)

brayperm
wuniperm
```

Formatting the table to look good, and easier to copy and paste into excel for manuscript formatting
```{r}
# Bray-Curtis table
bray_tab <- as.data.frame(brayperm)

bray_tab$Metric <- "Bray-Curtis"
bray_tab$Test <- rownames(bray_tab)

# Weighted UniFrac table
wuni_tab <- as.data.frame(wuniperm)

wuni_tab$Metric <- "Weighted UniFrac"
wuni_tab$Test <- rownames(wuni_tab)

# Combine
perm_tab <- rbind(bray_tab, wuni_tab)

perm_tab <- perm_tab[, c(
  "Metric",
  "Test",
  "Df",
  "SumOfSqs",
  "R2",
  "F",
  "Pr(>F)"
)]

colnames(perm_tab) <- c(
  "Metric",
  "Test",
  "Df",
  "Sum of squares",
  "R2",
  "F",
```

Because the habitat-stage factor (which is really the interaction of type and time), was dependent on treatment we will split by time to separate the effect of treatment on soil vs. plant associated.

### PERMANOVAs, dispersion, ANOSIM for each time point (i.e., stage)

```{r}
# ==========================================================
# SUBSET PHYLOSEQ OBJECT BY TIME
# ==========================================================

planting <- subset_samples(
  BSpermosphere_RDS_CSS,
  Time == "Planting"
)

h17 <- subset_samples(
  BSpermosphere_RDS_CSS,
  Time == "17hrs"
)

v2 <- subset_samples(
  BSpermosphere_RDS_CSS,
  Time == "V2"
)

# ==========================================================
# FUNCTION TO RUN PERMANOVA, DISPERSION, AND ANOSIM
# ==========================================================

run_multivar <- function(ps.obj,
                         distance = "bray",
                         perms = 999){

  # Distance matrix
  dist.mat <- phyloseq::distance(
    ps.obj,
    method = distance
  )

  meta <- data.frame(sample_data(ps.obj))

  # PERMANOVA
  perm <- adonis2(
    dist.mat ~ Trt * Type,
    data = meta,
    by = "term",
    permutations = perms
  )

  # DISPERSION
  meta$TrtType <- interaction(
    meta$Trt,
    meta$Type,
    drop = TRUE
  )

  disp <- betadisper(
    dist.mat,
    meta$TrtType
  )

  disp.aov <- anova(disp)

  # ANOSIM
  ano <- anosim(
    dist.mat,
    grouping = meta$TrtType,
    permutations = perms
  )

  return(
    list(
      permanova = perm,
      dispersion = disp.aov,
      anosim = ano
    )
  )
}

# ==========================================================
# RUN BRAY-CURTIS ANALYSES
# ==========================================================

planting.bray <- run_multivar(
  planting,
  distance = "bray"
)

h17.bray <- run_multivar(
  h17,
  distance = "bray"
)

v2.bray <- run_multivar(
  v2,
  distance = "bray"
)

# ==========================================================
# RUN WEIGHTED UNIFRAC ANALYSES
# ==========================================================

planting.wuni <- run_multivar(
  planting,
  distance = "wunifrac"
)

h17.wuni <- run_multivar(
  h17,
  distance = "wunifrac"
)

v2.wuni <- run_multivar(
  v2,
  distance = "wunifrac"
)

# ==========================================================
# FUNCTION TO FORMAT RESULTS TABLE
# ==========================================================

make_permanova_table <- function(res,
                                 metric,
                                 time){

  perm.df <- as.data.frame(res$permanova)

  perm.df$Test <- rownames(perm.df)

  perm.df <- perm.df[, c(
    "Test",
    "Df",
    "SumOfSqs",
    "R2",
    "F",
    "Pr(>F)"
  )]

  colnames(perm.df) <- c(
    "Test",
    "Df",
    "Sum of squares",
    "R2",
    "F",
    "Pr(>F)"
  )

  # Clean labels
  perm.df$Test <- recode(
    perm.df$Test,
    "Trt" = "Treatment",
    "Type" = "Habitat",
    "Trt:Type" = "Treatment × Habitat"
  )

  # Round values
  perm.df$`Sum of squares` <- round(
    perm.df$`Sum of squares`,
    4
  )

  perm.df$R2 <- round(
    perm.df$R2,
    3
  )

  perm.df$F <- round(
    perm.df$F,
    3
  )

  perm.df$Metric <- metric
  perm.df$Time <- time

  # Initialize columns
  perm.df$`Dispersion F` <- NA
  perm.df$`Dispersion Pr(>F)` <- NA
  perm.df$`ANOSIM R` <- NA
  perm.df$`ANOSIM Pr(>F)` <- NA

  # Add diagnostics to first row only
  perm.df$`Dispersion F`[1] <-
    round(
      res$dispersion$`F value`[1],
      3
    )

  perm.df$`Dispersion Pr(>F)`[1] <-
    round(
      res$dispersion$`Pr(>F)`[1],
      3
    )

  perm.df$`ANOSIM R`[1] <-
    round(
      as.numeric(res$anosim$statistic),
      3
    )

  perm.df$`ANOSIM Pr(>F)`[1] <-
    res$anosim$signif

  perm.df <- perm.df[, c(
    "Metric",
    "Time",
    "Test",
    "Df",
    "Sum of squares",
    "R2",
    "F",
    "Pr(>F)",
    "Dispersion F",
    "Dispersion Pr(>F)",
    "ANOSIM R",
    "ANOSIM Pr(>F)"
  )]

  return(perm.df)
}

# ==========================================================
# FORMAT BRAY-CURTIS TABLES
# ==========================================================

planting.bray.tab <- make_permanova_table(
  planting.bray,
  metric = "Bray-Curtis",
  time = "Planting"
)

h17.bray.tab <- make_permanova_table(
  h17.bray,
  metric = "Bray-Curtis",
  time = "17 h"
)

v2.bray.tab <- make_permanova_table(
  v2.bray,
  metric = "Bray-Curtis",
  time = "V2"
)

# ==========================================================
# FORMAT WEIGHTED UNIFRAC TABLES
# ==========================================================

planting.wuni.tab <- make_permanova_table(
  planting.wuni,
  metric = "Weighted-UniFrac",
  time = "Planting"
)

h17.wuni.tab <- make_permanova_table(
  h17.wuni,
  metric = "Weighted-UniFrac",
  time = "17 h"
)

v2.wuni.tab <- make_permanova_table(
  v2.wuni,
  metric = "Weighted-UniFrac",
  time = "V2"
)

# ==========================================================
# COMBINE ALL RESULTS
# ==========================================================

final.table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  planting.bray.tab,
  h17.bray.tab,
  v2.bray.tab,
  planting.wuni.tab,
  h17.wuni.tab,
  v2.wuni.tab
)

# ==========================================================
# VIEW RESULTS
# ==========================================================
final.table[is.na(final.table)] <- "–"
knitr::kable(final.table)

wb <- createWorkbook()

addWorksheet(wb, "Supplemental Table 4")

writeData(
  wb,
  sheet = 1,
  x = "Supplemental Table 4. PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, and ANOSIM results testing 
  the effects of steaming treatment, habitat, and their interaction on bacterial 
  community composition."
)

writeData(
  wb,
  sheet = 1,
  x = final.table,
  startRow = 3
)

saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  "Supplemental_Table_4.xlsx",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```


```{r}
make_pcoa_df <- function(ps.obj,
                         distance = "bray") {

  dist.mat <- phyloseq::distance(
    ps.obj,
    method = distance
  )

  ord <- ordinate(
    ps.obj,
    method = "PCoA",
    distance = dist.mat
  )

  pcoa.df <- plot_ordination(
    ps.obj,
    ord,
    justDF = TRUE
  )

  eig <- ord$values$Relative_eig * 100

  list(
    data = pcoa.df,
    axis1 = round(eig[1], 2),
    axis2 = round(eig[2], 2)
  )
}

```


```{r}
make_panel <- function(
    pcoa.res,
    title,
    p.value
){

  ggplot(
    pcoa.res$data,
    aes(
      Axis.1,
      Axis.2,
      fill = Trt,
      shape = Type
    )
  ) +

    geom_point(
      size = 2,
      colour = "black",
      alpha = 0.7
    ) +

    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Non.Steamed" = "black",
        "Steamed " = "#E69F00"
      )
    ) +

    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c(
        "Bulk.Soil" = 21,
        "Spermosphere" = 24,
        "Rhizosphere" = 25
      )
    ) +

    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = paste0(
        "Treatment × Habitat p = ",
        p.value
      ),

      x = paste0(
        "PcoA1 - ",
        pcoa.res$axis1,
        " %"
      ),

      y = paste0(
        "PcoA2 - ",
        pcoa.res$axis2,
        " %"
      )
    ) +

    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +

    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10)
    )
}
```

```{r}
get_interaction_p <- function(res){

  p <- as.data.frame(res$permanova)["Trt:Type", "Pr(>F)"]

  if(p < 0.001){
    return("< 0.001")
  } else {
    return(sprintf("%.3f", p))
  }

}

p1 <- make_panel(
  bray.planting,
  "Planting",
  get_interaction_p(planting.bray)
)

p2 <- make_panel(
  bray.h17,
  "17 Hours Postplanting",
  get_interaction_p(h17.bray)
)

p3 <- make_panel(
  bray.v2,
  "V2 Growth Stage",
  get_interaction_p(v2.bray)
)

p4 <- make_panel(
  wu.planting,
  "Planting",
  get_interaction_p(planting.wuni)
)

p5 <- make_panel(
  wu.h17,
  "17 Hours Postplanting",
  get_interaction_p(h17.wuni)
)

p6 <- make_panel(
  wu.v2,
  "V2 Growth Stage",
  get_interaction_p(v2.wuni)
)
```
